text:
Jamie (Support): Hey team — customer Gridline reports ~3k objects that should have been deleted after TTL but still show up in search. They say TTL expired 2026-11-01. Customer IDs: obj_9a8b7c, obj_9a8b7d, obj_9a8b7e. Can we confirm deletion pipeline?

Alex M.: assigning. do we have repro steps from the customer? sample curl/response?

Jamie (Support): they sent this quick repro: `curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer <token>\" https://api.prod.redwood.ai/v1/objects/obj_9a8b7c` -> 200 with payload (object present). They also attached a screenshot of search results. No legal hold flags from customer side.

Maria - SRE: quick checks: is deletion worker crashing on KMS decrypt? or tombstone write failing to index. please share audit log id if available. I'll tail the deletion-queue.

SRE Bot: [alert] retention-scheduler job failed 2026-11-02T03:04:12Z -> error: "queue_lock_timeout". retries: 5. job_id=ret-sched-20261102-03

Alex M.: thanks — that matches an infra alert I saw. Maria, what's backlog size?

Maria - SRE: backlog snapshot (from prod):
```
> SELECT count(*) FROM deletion_queue WHERE status = 'pending';
 count
-------
 3124
```
backlog ~= 3.1k pending. worker processes were flapping between 03:00-03:15 UTC. logs show repeated lock timeouts.

Dan O.: any KMS/HSM errors in the same window? KMS latency would cause tombstone commit retries.

Maria - SRE: pulled KMS audit: no explicit customer HSM holds. There are a few transient 5xx decrypts at 03:02:05Z and 03:06:10Z. sample: `KMS: decrypt error: 503 Backend overloaded` for key id rk-prod-3.

Jamie (Support): customer insists no holds. they're asking for an expedited purge if we can't get automatic deletes working. legal hold?

Legal Ops: Not aware of any legal hold for Gridline org. Please confirm with cust before purge — need confirmation in ticket and audit trail.

Alex M.: proposed mitigation path: 1) pause scheduler to avoid double-processing, 2) kick manual worker run on a controlled subset (IDs provided), 3) if delete API still errors due to KMS, consult infra for KMS throttling relief, 4) if customer approves, run force-delete that writes a tombstone + audit entry and purges from search index. Need approver + audit id.

Maria - SRE: I can run controlled retry for the 3 sample objects now. repro commands I'll run:
```
curl -X POST https://internal-admin.prod.redwood.ai/v1/delete/retry \
  -H "X-Admin-Token: <redacted>" \
  -d '{"object_ids": ["obj_9a8b7c","obj_9a8b7d","obj_9a8b7e"]}'
```
I'll tail logs: `kubectl logs -l app=deletion-worker --since=10m` and watch for `tombstone_written` events.

SRE Bot: job ret-sched-20261102-03: queued manual_recovery by Maria - SRE.

Maria - SRE: running now — small log snippet: 
```
[03:12:01Z] deletion-worker/0 processing obj_9a8b7c
[03:12:02Z] tombstone_written obj_9a8b7c shard=42
[03:12:03Z] index_purge_enqueued obj_9a8b7c
[03:12:03Z] deletion-api: KMS decrypt attempt 1 -> 503
[03:12:05Z] deletion-api: KMS decrypt attempt 2 -> success
[03:12:06Z] deletion-complete obj_9a8b7c
```
So sample objects successfully deleted after retry. there are intermittent kms 503s causing earlier failures.

Dan O.: looks like root cause = KMS transient overload causing deletion worker retries and eventual backlog. Are we sure deletion worker had correct exponential backoff? Could saturating retries create lock timeouts?

Alex M.: yes, combination of retry storms + queue_lock_timeout. we should patch scheduler to use jittered backoff and limit concurrent decrypt attempts per key. ticket infra.

Jamie (Support): customer wants ETA and whether their data was exposed in search while marked for deletion. what's the message to send?

Maria - SRE: from our logs, between 2026-11-01T00:00:00Z and 2026-11-02T03:12:00Z those objects were still readable by API/search. tombstone written only at 03:12:02Z for sample. we need to run a full scan to compute exact window for affected object set.

Alex M.: suggested reply to cust: explain transient KMS error caused delay, confirm no legal hold, propose manual purge for remaining backlog items within next 2 hours, offer audit log export and deletion confirmation CSV. ask for explicit approval to run force-delete tool.

Legal Ops: If customer signs approval in ticket, we need to record: approver name, timestamp, scope (object IDs or whole org), and reason. we'll attach audit record and retention policy version used.

Jamie (Support): I'll draft reply and request approval. also asking billing to hold any retention-related billing adjustments until resolution.

Maria - SRE: next steps I'm taking: 1) continue controlled retries for high-priority IDs, 2) run a job to reprocess oldest 3k pending items in small batches with backoff, 3) open infra ticket to throttle decrypt concurrency per key.

SRE Bot: incident created: INC-2026-7843 -> retention: deletion-backlog-kms-throttle. priority P2. assigned: eng-infra.

Alex M.: tagging @Dan O. please coordinate KMS throughput change with cloud team. Also add a postmortem once resolved.

Dan O.: on it. I'll review KMS metric graphs and request short-term throttle raise + alert thresholds.

Jamie (Support): customer updated ticket saying they'll approve manual purge for listed object IDs only. I've captured approver name (Ellen R.) and timestamp 2026-11-02T04:01:10Z. Legal Ops, please confirm this is sufficient.

Legal Ops: that's fine for those object IDs. ensure audit CSV includes the approver signature line and ticket id.

Maria - SRE: performed manual purge for the 3 sample objects. I'll post CSV and audit id when available.

Jamie (Support): thanks all — I'll send customer final note once audit CSV posted. marking as in-progress. :thumbsup:
